There is no formula that every source agrees on. What the sources here do
agree on is what a bad limit looks like:

- **Too high.** A limit of 20 for a team of five does not constrain anything;
  it writes down the overload the team already has ([[anderson:wip-limits]]).
- **Ignored.** When a column keeps hitting its limit, the temptation is to
  raise the limit. That hides the bottleneck the limit was exposing
  ([[anderson:wip-limits]]).
- **On invisible work.** A limit needs a visible board first: you cannot
  enforce a cap on work nobody can see ([[anderson:wip-limits]]).

Not verified: a starting number. Treat any "team size plus one" or "two per
person" rule as an opening guess to adjust, not a finding.

See also [[wip-limits-in-practice]] and [[reinertsen:wip-constraints]].
